correctness.rationale: For the specified compact binary-shift quotient, classify large-time orbit transition pairs: p may go to any target; an x rising front can approach p or a falling y front; a y front can approach p or a rising x; a finite island can approach only p. Growing island blocks realize opposite-front arcs, and inverse shifts realize p->target; a finite list of arcs is realized at the same diverging times with distinct source configurations. A nonwandering A in F_n yields, after convergent point assignments and m_j tending to infinity unless A={p}, an in/out-cover of A using at most n distinct arcs. The converse realizes any such edge cover simultaneously. Bipartite edge-cover theorem gives min size 2|A|-maximum_matching, with infinity when isolated on either side. A={p,two distinct islands} has threshold 4. Independently enumerated small matching/edge-cover examples; not exhaustive dynamic verification.
